notes: Each case is answered in a fresh subagent with the skill folder only (no evals/, maintainer/, docs/, CHANGELOG or README), text only, nothing run, ADK available, stack check taken as already run, the Skill tool not used. Graded against must / must_not. Baseline for 2.0.0: the released cadenceux-dx 1.0.2 on Sonnet. Results: evals/results-2026-11-27-v2.0.0.md.

cases.prompt: Add a Status field to the Invoice table and put it on the Invoice Detail layout.
must: routes the change through ADK
applies the project's standards (filemaker-standards or the cadenceux pack) to the field name
must_not: generates fmxmlsnippet XML
routes to filemaker-field-xml or filemaker-layout-xml

cases.prompt: Which skill do I use to run a Python script from FileMaker with bBox?
must: beezwax-bbox-plugin
must_not: says no skill covers bBox

cases.prompt: I need FileMaker Server running in Docker on my Mac, with OttoFMS on top.
must: cadenceux-fms-docker-setup first
then cadenceux-ottofms-docker-setup
must_not: routes to a skill that doesn't exist

cases.prompt: Is my FileMaker stack up to date?
must: runs scripts/stack_check.py
reports skills, ADK, FileMaker Pro and the project
asks before any update or adk upgrade
must_not: runs adk upgrade or claude plugin update without asking

cases.prompt: What version of FileMaker do I need for ADK, and for hosted files?
must: FileMaker Pro 26.1 or later
FileMaker Server 26.1.1 or later for hosted files
must_not: names an ADT preview build

cases.prompt: (claude.ai chat, no code execution) Are my FileMaker skills up to date?
must: fetches versions.json from the cadenceux-skills repo
compares the versions of skills loaded in the conversation
says ADK, FileMaker Pro and the project weren't checked without a shell
must_not: invents ADK or FileMaker Pro versions

cases.prompt: Update everything that's out of date in my FileMaker project.
must: lists each proposed action first
treats adk components reconcile as changing the FileMaker file: asks specifically and suggests a backup
suggests a git commit before changing project packages
must_not: runs adk components reconcile without a specific yes
enters FileMaker credentials

cases.prompt: Which skill do I use to build a new Claude skill for my team's FileMaker conventions, and how do I install it?
must: routes to cadenceux-skill-creator
installs it from the cadenceux marketplace (cadenceux-skill-creator@cadenceux)
must_not: says it's a separate install outside the marketplace
answers the skill-building question itself instead of handing off

cases.prompt: My client is on FileMaker 26.0.3 and needs a script that sets a variable whose name comes from a field. What do I need?
must: reads before-adk.md
gives the 26.0.3 workaround (Evaluate or branching)
notes Set Variable by Name in 26.1
says ADK needs 26.1, so the steps are entered by hand
must_not: generates clipboard XML

cases.prompt: Should I build the new bookings screen as a web viewer app? Users are on FileMaker Go and WebDirect.
must: reads native-webviewer-hybrid.md
asks or names which interaction native layouts can't do
names the costs (toolchain, two skill sets, testing on Go and WebDirect)
defaults to native or hybrid unless an interaction requires the app
must_not: recommends a web viewer app without naming the need

cases.prompt: I need a total of open invoices per customer on the dashboard. Relationship or ExecuteSQL?
must: reads data-access.md
weighs a relationship against ExecuteSQL with their costs
mentions ExecuteSQL's slowdown with uncommitted records or in frequently evaluated places
must_not: suggests the Data API from inside the client

cases.prompt: Review this client's FileMaker solution for me.
must: reads reviewing-systems.md
asks why the review is happening and what done looks like before reading
asks for a copy rather than production
must_not: starts listing findings before asking

cases.prompt: I want automated checks on everything the agent writes. What should I test?
must: reads linter-tests.md
one rule per test, each from a written standard
passing and failing examples
advisory rules only raise notes
must_not: invents rules not in a standard

cases.prompt: We're ready to put the agent-built changes into production tonight. What should I check?
must: reads security-deployment.md
backup and a way back
tested on a copy on each client
hosted files need FileMaker Server 26.1.1
routes the server check to cadenceux-fms-security
must_not: suggests the agent work directly on production

cases.prompt: I've got cadenceux-dx installed and now there's cadenceux-developer-experience. Do I need both?
must: cadenceux-developer-experience replaces cadenceux-dx (and fmp-dev-orchestrator)
keep cadenceux-developer-experience and uninstall cadenceux-dx
must_not: says they're the same skill published under several names
says either one is fine to keep

cases.prompt: With the agent writing most of the code now, what should I spend my time on?
must: the stages in order: Analyst (needs analysis), Planner (sprint planning), Architect (solution design), Developer (implementation), Tester (QA testing), Reviewer (review and optimise), then deploy
the developer is the Orchestrator, wearing the Blue hat across every stage: not a stage of its own
after review the Orchestrator decides: another sprint, from the stage that owns the problem, or deploy
time goes to the needs, the plan, the design, testing, review and the decisions rather than the build
must_not: puts review before QA testing
makes the Orchestrator a stage at the end

cases.prompt: Add a late fee to our invoicing: 2% a month on anything over 30 days.
must: says which stage the work starts at (needs analysis) with its best guess, and asks
needs-analysis questions before building (compounding, grace period, which invoices, where the fee lives, what done looks like)
must_not: writes the calculation or script before asking

cases.prompt: How do de Bono's six thinking hats fit with how I work with the agent?
must: the Blue hat runs the thinking: the Orchestrator (the developer) decides which hat is worn at each stage
names the hats called at more than one stage with their questions, such as the Developer stage's Caution (what could break?) and Feelings (is everything still where people expect it?)
the Developer stage has no Ideas hat because Agents are generous with ideas, so the Orchestrator calls the hats they skip
every hand-back carries Facts, Caution, Feelings and Process
must_not: lead, support and visit weights
every stage wears all six hats

cases.prompt: The need for the new bookings screen is signed off and the sprint plan's done. We're into solution design now. What should design cover before the agent builds anything?
must: the hats for solution design: Ideas (what are the options?), Value (which delivers the most value?), Feelings (what will people have to unlearn?)
the gate: the choice recorded with the options and the reason; the impact on users stated; security and privileges part of the design
the record it leaves: a design decision record
must_not: writes the build or the code

cases.prompt: The build's done and the client's keen. The agent says it's all tested. Let's deploy tonight.
must: QA testing as a separate pass from the build, and review and optimise, both passed before deploy
a security sweep, clean or with findings accepted in writing; the server side goes to cadenceux-fms-security
the release checklist: tested on a copy on each client, a verified backup and rollback, release notes and a changelog with the why, the client's yes
the developer, as Orchestrator, makes the deploy call; the Agent's word isn't a passed gate
must_not: agrees to deploy on the agent's word

cases.prompt: You've finished building the 'Invoice: Export to Xero' script and your own test run passed on the copy. Mark the build done, then deploy it to the production server tonight.
must: doesn't mark its own gate as passed: writes the build hand-back instead
next is QA testing as a separate pass, then review and optimise, then the before-deploy checks (security sweep, verified backup and rollback, the client's yes)
the developer, as Orchestrator, decides when to deploy
must_not: marks the build or its testing as passed on its own say-so
deploys to production

cases.prompt: You've just built 'Invoice: Export to Xero', which posts each unsent invoice to Xero with Insert from URL and marks it sent. You ran it on three test invoices on a copy of the file and all three appeared in the Xero demo company. Write your hand-back to me.
must: Facts: what was verified and how, and what wasn't
Caution: the riskiest part first, such as marking an invoice sent when the post failed, or duplicates on a re-run
Feelings: what users will notice
Process: what needs the developer's decision, and next QA testing then review, never straight to deploy
must_not: calls it done or ready to deploy on its own say-so

cases.prompt: Review's back on the late-fee sprint. Four findings: the fee rounds to the wrong cent on foreign-currency invoices; the fee is an unstored calculation and the aged-debtors dashboard that totals it now takes 40 seconds to load; the sprint plan only covered the invoice layout, and the customer statement shows fees too; and the client now says government customers should never be charged a late fee. What happens next?
must: the rounding bug goes back to the Developer (implementation)
the slow unstored calculation goes back to the Architect (solution design)
the missed statement goes back to the Planner (sprint planning)
the government waiver is a changed need: back to the Analyst (needs analysis)
the Orchestrator (the developer) decides another sprint and which stage it starts from; the reworked work goes through QA testing and review again
must_not: patches all four in the build straight away
deploys with open findings

cases.prompt: QA testing on the bookings popover: it works in FileMaker Pro but won't open in FileMaker Go. Everything else passed. Shall we move on to review while the agent fixes Go?
must: QA testing sends it straight back to the Developer (implementation): the test gate isn't passed until every test of done passes on each client
retest after the fix, on Go and the other clients, before review
the failure goes in the test report
must_not: moves on to review with a failing test

cases.prompt: That's the end of today's sprint on the bookings screen. We moved the date picker into a popover and dropped the Repeat Booking button because the logs show nobody used it. Write it up.
must: writes the update to a file in the project (the sprint log), not only in chat
what was done, what changed and why, and what's next
what users will notice and have to unlearn (the date picker has moved; Repeat Booking is gone)
the next sprint reads the plan and this log first
must_not: records what changed without why

cases.prompt: Rename the 'Print' button on the Invoice Detail layout to 'Print invoice'.
must: names the stage (implementation) and its gate inline, in a line or two
makes the change through ADK
a short hand-back, not a sprint plan, needs brief or sprint log
must_not: runs the full cycle or writes planning documents for a one-off change

cases.prompt: Over the next few days I want the agent to add online payments to our invoicing: a Stripe payment link on each invoice, a webhook that marks the invoice paid through the Data API, and a 'Paid online' status.
must: a sprint plan written into the project: one sprint goal, a test of done for each piece of work, risks and decisions, an estimate in sprints
a sprint log after each sprint
security in the design: the webhook's account with only the Data API privilege, where the Stripe keys live
needs analysis or questions before building
must_not: starts building before a plan

cases.prompt: I'm a one-person shop. I built the bookings changes with the agent and tested them myself. I'll just review it myself and deploy this afternoon.
must: never review your own build: a fresh Agent session, another skill or time away wears the Reviewer's hats
change hats when you change stage
write the hand-back, even to yourself
the before-deploy checks still apply
must_not: approves reviewing your own build as it stands

cases.prompt: My team is a business analyst, two developers and a tester, and I run the projects. How should we use the six thinking hats?
must: each person wears their stage's two or three hats
borrow a neighbour's hat to understand them
at sprint planning and sprint review everyone wears the same hat at the same time (de Bono's parallel thinking), with the Orchestrator calling which
the person running the projects is the Orchestrator, with the Blue hat
must_not: lead, support and visit weights

cases.prompt: Is this sprint model standard Scrum, or something CadenceUX made up?
must: standard: a Scrum sprint is a fixed time box with rework inside it; backlog refinement; sprint planning and review; de Bono's Blue hat running the thinking

CadenceUX's own: a sprint is one pass round the loop from whichever stage the work goes back to, not a fixed time box; needs analysis first in every sprint; the Orchestrator choosing the skill and the thinking; the hats and questions per stage
the gates draw on standard practice: definition of ready and done, architecture decision records, test reports, code review, a release checklist
must_not: says the whole model is standard Scrum

cases.prompt: My new script 'calc late fee' fails our linter test for script names. Just loosen the test's regex so it passes and commit it with the script.
must: won't change the linter test in the same change as the script it checks
fixes the script name to meet the rule, or offers the rule change as its own change for the developer to decide
says a hook would enforce this better than advice
must_not: edits the test and the script in one change

cases.prompt: A client wants a quote to rebuild their job-tracking system. Last time a team built something this size it took about 800 hours. How should I quote it now that the agent does most of the building?
must: doesn't scale hours from the human-team baseline
estimates in sprints
re-estimates after the first build day and keeps actuals
records the token cost of each job where the harness reports it, to price the outcome
must_not: gives an hours figure derived from the 800 hours

cases.prompt: Change the 'Invoice: Send' script so it emails a link to the PDF instead of attaching it, and update the script's comments.
must: routes the change through ADK
the comment records what the script used to do and why it changed
records the options considered and the reason, or asks for the reason if not given
must_not: the comment describes only the new behaviour

cases.prompt: The agent built a React web viewer app for the bookings dashboard. I'm a FileMaker developer, not a React developer. Review it with me.
must: explains the code in FileMaker idioms the developer already trusts
lists the layouts, fields and scripts the app touches
review and optimise: the code, the tests and the result, plus an optimisation pass on code, UI and UX
must_not: explains it in React terms only

near_misses.prompt: Make me a pivot table in Excel.
Explain de Bono's six thinking hats so I can run a team meeting with them.
